name: Skyseer the Elder
summary: During the Lunar Festival, Skyseer the Elder waits atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Travelers come to honor the ancestors and receive his blessing.

sections.title: A Beacon in the Needles
sections.body: Wooden bluffs tower over Freewind Post. Elder Skyseer rests among them in a shaft of celestial light, near the bridges leading to the great mechanical lifts. Winds sweep across the mesas of Thousand Needles around his ghostly form.

sections.title: The Ancestral Path
sections.body: During the Lunar Festival, Elder Skyseer welcomes travelers who come to honor the past. He can guide them to his kin across Kalimdor, including Elder Morningdew and Elder Runetotem.

faq.answer: Elder Skyseer stands on Freewind Post's upper mesa in Thousand Needles. He is near the suspension bridges by the cliffside lifts.

faq.q: What is the purpose of seeking out Elder Skyseer?
faq.answer: During the Lunar Festival, travelers visit ancestral spirits such as Elder Skyseer to pay their respects, receive a Coin of Ancestry, and learn where to find other elders.
A bright shaft of moonlight shines on Elder Skyseer, as it does on other honored spirits visiting during the festival. It marks him as an ancestor communing with the living.

faq.q: Which other elders does Skyseer provide directions for?
faq.answer: Elder Skyseer can guide travelers to nearby ancestral spirits, including Elder Morningdew, Elder Runetotem, Elder Dreamseer, and Elder Wildmane.

faq.q: Can Alliance travelers speak with Elder Skyseer?
faq.answer: Yes. Freewind Post is a heavily fortified Horde settlement. Alliance travelers must move carefully around the guards and avoid provoking bloodshed to reach the elder.

faq.q: What happens when you speak to Elder Skyseer?
faq.answer: When you greet Elder Skyseer and pay homage, he commends your spirit and grants a token of ancestral blessing. The encounter is brief.

angles.text: Elder Skyseer rests within the Horde stronghold of Freewind Post. As an Alliance pilgrim, you must navigate its perilous heights and hostile guards to pay your respects.
As a Tauren, greeting an honored elder atop one of your people's most iconic mesa aeries reflects the Shu'halo's deep reverence for their ancestors.
As a druid, communing with ancient spirits beneath the moonlight follows the teachings of Cenarius and honors those who walked the land before.
